html:
A battle fought on 26 August 1071 near Manzikert, north of Lake Van in eastern Anatolia, in which the Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan defeated the Byzantine emperor Romanos IV Diogenes and took him prisoner.

Romanos had marched east with a large but mixed army to stop Turkish raids into Anatolia. Part of his force was away when the battle came. The Turks used their usual tactic of retreating while shooting arrows, drawing the Byzantines on. As Romanos turned back at dusk, his rear guard under Andronikos Doukas, a political rival, withdrew, and the army broke. The emperor was captured, the first Byzantine emperor ever taken prisoner by a Muslim ruler.

Alp Arslan treated him well and freed him on fair terms. But at home Romanos had already been deposed, and he was blinded and died. The civil wars that followed left Anatolia open, and Turkmen tribes moved in and settled. Within twenty years the empire had lost most of the region, and Emperor Alexios I asked the West for help, which led to the First Crusade.
